modelOverview: Presented at Baselworld 2018, the Nautilus 5740 is the first Grand Complication in the Nautilus collection, fitting a full perpetual calendar with moon phases into the familiar rounded-octagonal case and integrated bracelet. It is built around the ultra-thin micro-rotor Calibre 240 Q, which keeps the case to just 8.42mm thick despite displaying day, date, month, leap year, 24-hour indication and moon phases across three sub-dials. Patek Philippe has offered it in 18k white gold with a sunburst blue dial since launch.

5740/1G-001.movement: Automatic · Patek Philippe Calibre 240 Q · 21,600 vph · 38–48h power reserve
5740/1G-001.materials: 18k white gold case and integrated bracelet with patented fold-over clasp
5740/1G-001.bezel: White gold rounded-octagonal Nautilus bezel with contrasting polished and satin-brushed finishes
5740/1G-001.dial: Sunburst blue dial with horizontal embossing, white gold applied baton hour markers and rounded baton hands with white luminescent coating; day and 24-hour sub-dial at 9 o'clock, month and leap-year sub-dial at 3 o'clock, date and moon phases at 6 o'clock
5740/1G-001.description: The 5740/1G-001 brings a perpetual calendar with moon phases to the Nautilus for the first time, using the micro-rotor Calibre 240 Q to keep the white gold case remarkably slim at 8.42mm. The three-register layout sits on the collection's signature horizontally embossed sunburst blue dial, with a sapphire caseback showing the 22k gold micro-rotor and the Patek Philippe Seal movement. Every piece we offer is sourced and independently authenticated before sale.

variants.White Gold – Blue Dial: 5740/1G-001 in 18k white gold on its integrated white gold bracelet with the sunburst blue embossed dial, the sole configuration of the Nautilus Perpetual Calendar since its 2018 launch.
